nodes.name: Receive Inbound Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point: listens for POST calls on /wf09168-order. Use the TEST url while building, switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after publishing. Watch out: While building use the TEST url; switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after you publish.

nodes.name: Pull Side A (MySQL)
nodes.notes: Selects rows from the MySQL table (returnAll) — the read side of the store. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Pull Side B (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Order Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Diff the Two Systems
nodes.notes: Diffs two streams by key into 4 lanes: only-in-A, same, different, only-in-B — the heart of the sync.

nodes.name: Create Missing in Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Order Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Count In-Sync Rows
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Apply Updates to Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Order Tracker', matched on orderId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Backfill into MySQL
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Gather Sync Results
nodes.notes: Rejoins 4 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per order (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Fulfill new orders with Shopify and MySQL

**Pattern:** Order Fulfillment · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Webhook

## What it does
Fulfill new orders with Shopify and MySQL. It fires the moment an external system calls its webhook.

## Why it exists
Manual order ops is slow and error-prone; this workflow makes the process repeatable, monitored and hands-off, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow
Receive Inbound Webhook → Pull Side A (MySQL) → Diff the Two Systems → Create Missing in Google Sheets → Gather Sync Results → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → …

## Use it for
- Teams that want to order fulfillment without manual effort
- Anyone automating order ops in e-commerce
- Replacing a fragile manual process with a reliable workflow

## You get
- Improves response time
- Standardizes the process every time
- Runs 24/7 in the background

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Discord webhook URL; Google OAuth2 / service account; MySQL connection.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Compare Datasets does the matching instead of hand-rolled join logic — one node produces four labeled lanes (only-in-A, matching, different, only-in-B), and each lane gets exactly the action it needs (create / count / update / backfill) instead of one generic 'sync' branch trying to cover every case.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Swap Side A or Side B for a third platform and rewire the merge-by-fields key.
2. Intentionally create a mismatch between the two systems and trace which lane it lands in.
3. Change mergeByFields to a different key and see how the diff results shift.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Never trust inbound payloads: the webhook path is unguessable. Add header auth or IP allow-listing for defense in depth. Secrets live in n8n credentials — never in node parameters.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your order ops process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
